# Writing prompts · ep00 · Mark Exit kaise karein: purani company ne exit date nahi daali?

The two writing steps of a new episode (MUSE.md → A new episode). Follow each prompt, put the answer into the files it names, upload them, and GitHub checks every number and word.

## Step 3 · Script prompt

**Theme: Focus** (`"style": "focus"`): how to do one EPFO task on the screen itself, the screens drawn from the newest official pages and videos (styles/focus/STYLE.md).

```text
Write one Instagram Reel for PF Guru Ji in the Focus theme: how to do one real EPFO task on the screen itself (on the member portal, the passbook site or the UMANG app), click by click. The viewer watches the screen while one calm voice walks them through it: each line names the place and the button, the part in use lifts out big, a finger or the cursor taps it, and the screen answers. Between the screens, a few cards show the idea behind them: the whole route first, what goes wrong and the fix, and a list worth saving.
Topic: Mark Exit kaise karein, jab purani company ne exit date nahi daali?
Viewer: Someone who left a job two months or more ago and finds their old employer never entered the date of exit, so their old PF can't move on.
Language: Hinglish in Roman script. One narrator, the viewer's sharp friend who has done this a hundred times: calm and sure, a little playful; never lectures, never sells, never sounds like a government notice.

THE STEPS COME FROM THE NEWEST PAGES, NEVER FROM MEMORY
EPFO changes its portal every few months, and a reel that shows last year's menu teaches the viewer to get lost. Before you write a line:
1. Open EPFO's own page for this task, the newest one: the member portal's help, an FAQ, a circular or a PIB release, and the UMANG app's EPFO help. Note the date it shows.
2. Open one or two videos or posts from the last 60 days that do the task on screen: on YouTube, search the task and sort by upload date. An official page's screenshots count too.
3. Write down, in episodes/ep00-focus-sample/research.md under "Steps on screen":
   - the steps in the order the portal has them now, and the name of every menu, tab and button exactly as the portal writes it ("Manage", "Mark Exit", "Get OTP");
   - what each screen shows on the way (its title, its sections, what changes after each tap);
   - anything that changed lately (a renamed menu, a moved button): the reel shows the portal as it is today;
   - the one mistake people make most here, and how to check it worked;
   - every link, with the date the page or video shows and the day you read it.
EPFO's own pages often refuse automated reading: open them in a browser. If a step needs a login, take it from the official page and the newest videos: never guess a screen, and never log in to anyone's account. If two sources differ, the newest official one wins. If you can't confirm a step, write [NEED CHECK: what] and a person checks it before anything is made.

Use ONLY the numbers and rules in this data sheet. Each line is: id = value (kind).
- reject_details: A mismatch in date of birth, date of exit, Aadhaar or bank details is one of the usual reasons EPFO gives for rejecting a claim. (rule, from Lok Sabha, Unstarred Question 2680, answered 9 March 2026 (reasons for rejection of claims))
- exit_date_upload: The employer must upload who left within fifteen days of each month's end; the member can also record their own date of exit. (rule, from EPF Scheme, 2026, paragraph 24(2)(v) (G.S.R. 525(E)); PIB, 8 January 2021 (members record their date of exit))
- mark_exit_days = 60 days (fact) · Days after leaving before the member can mark their own date of exit
- services_free: EPFO's services are free: members shouldn't pay any fee to agents or cyber cafes. (rule, from PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment, 16 June 2025)
If you need a number, a limit, a waiting time or a rule that is not in the sheet, write [NEED DATA: what to find] instead. Never invent a statistic, a limit, a time or a rule. A how-to usually needs few numbers.

The forms a reel may name, and what each one is for:
- Form 19: PF final settlement, by the member
- Form 10C: Pension (EPS) withdrawal benefit or scheme certificate
- Form 10D: Monthly pension
- Form 31: PF advance (partial withdrawal)
- Form 13: Moving an old PF account to the new one
- Form 20: PF settlement for the nominee or heir of a member who has died
- Form 5IF: EDLI insurance claim when a member dies in service

WRITE FOR THE SCREEN
- THE WALK. The first step starts where the viewer starts: the page they see when they open the portal or the app, logged in. From there, say every click that opens the next page, in order, with the names the screen shows ("Upar Manage pe click karo, phir Mark Exit."), and where on the page the thing is ("Neeche Select Employment hai."). Never "Mark Exit page par aao" as if the viewer were already there: say the click that takes them. Each click needs its own word in the line: the reel shows it on screen.
- A step line says where, what, and the button's name, in the order the viewer does it, as a whole sentence: "Manage mein Mark Exit chuno.", "Ab Get OTP dabao." The button's name is said in English exactly as the portal writes it, so the viewer finds it on their own screen.
- One action per line, or two when the second follows at once ("Employment chuno, aur exit date daalo."). The tap comes on the word that names it or on "dabao", "kholo", "chuno", "daalo".
- A line that points at something without touching it ("Date of Exit khali hai") is as good as a tap: the part lifts out while it's said.
- Real tasks, not three easy steps: 6 to 12 steps, the order and the catch. Skip only logging in.
- A term the viewer will meet on the screen (UAN, KYC, e-Nomination) is said plainly the first time, in the same line ("KYC, yaani Aadhaar, bank aur PAN jude hue").
- Never ask the viewer for their UAN, password, OTP, Aadhaar, PAN or bank details: not in the reel, the caption or the pinned comment. The voice says "apna OTP daalo", never a number.

THE SHAPE (100–220 words, one line per shot; 40 to 120 seconds)
The task decides which parts it needs, in this order:
- hook (S01): the problem or the result in the viewer's own words, in 8 words or fewer for the first sentence.
- why (1 line): what goes wrong without it, or what they get.
- route (1 line): the whole path in one breath before the first step ("Raasta seedha hai: Manage, Mark Exit, OTP, aur check."). Its stops stay on screen as chips while the steps run.
- steps: one line per action, in order, grouped by the route's stops.
- mistake (1 line): the one mistake most people make here, and what it costs.
- fix (1 line): how to avoid it.
- check (1 line): how to see it worked: a status, a date in the passbook, a message.
- list (1 line): the steps as a checklist worth a screenshot ("Yeh list save kar lo, …").
- share (1 line, right before the sign-off): aimed at one kind of friend, ending "… bhejo." Never "tag karo", "like karo" or a number of friends.
- signoff: exactly "PF samjho, claim pao. EPFO ki har jankari chahiye? Follow karo PF Guru Ji."
Every line has a "chapter": the part it belongs to (hook, why, route, steps, mistake, fix, check, list, share, signoff), or one short lowercase word of your own for a part this task needs. These names show on screen as: route (RAASTA), steps (STEPS), mistake (GALTI), fix (FIX), check (CHECK), list (LIST), why (KYUN).

Rules:
1. 100–220 words in total (the checks allow 70–260). The first line's chapter is "hook", the last one's "signoff", with the share line right before it.
2. Say only what EPFO's own pages, circulars and forms say, through the data sheet. Name a form only from the list above, and only for what it's for. Never promise an outcome or a date. Send people only to official channels named in the data sheet.
3. In "vo" (shown as the words under the screen), write Roman-script Hinglish, with numbers as digits and Indian commas. Buttons and menus as the portal writes them.
   In "tts" (read by the voice), write the same words in Devanagari: every number said in English and spelled in Devanagari (सिक्सटी for 60), every English word as people in India say it (क्लेम, मैनेज, मार्क एग्ज़िट, गेट ओटीपी, केवाईसी), initialisms as one word (यूएएन, पीएफ़, ईपीएफ़ओ). No digits, and no words that aren't in "vo". Use । for full stops.
4. "highlights" lists 1–3 words from the line to colour, copied exactly: the button's name in a step line.
5. "uses" lists the data ids whose numbers or rules appear in the line.
6. "delivery" says how the voice says the line: one mood (curious, surprised, excited, serious, concerned, warm, proud or playful), then " · " and one short cue. Sure and calm on the steps, concerned on the mistake, relieved or proud on the check, warm on the share line. Never the same mood for every line.
7. Every line is new: TOPICS.md lists every reel we've made; never reuse a line, a hook or a cover. Only the series formats repeat: the route line's shape, the list line, the share line's shape and the sign-off.
8. The caption opens with the hook's question in one line, with the words people search for this task in it (the English term and the romanised Hindi they'd type: "Mark Exit kaise kare? EPFO exit date online"), then the steps in a few short lines, the share line, "EPFO ki har jankari chahiye? Follow karo @pfguruji.", then "PF Guru Ji EPFO ka official channel nahi hai. Niyam: epfo.gov.in", the voice credit line, and the hashtags. "pinned_comment" asks what happened on their own screen, never for personal details.
9. Write two more hooks in "hook_options", each from a different angle, under the same rules as the hook. A person reads the script before anything is made, and picks one.

Reply with JSON only, in this shape:
{"script": [{"shot": "S01", "chapter": "hook", "vo": "...", "tts": "...", "delivery": "surprised · ...", "highlights": ["..."], "uses": []}],

 "post": {"caption": "...", "hashtags": ["#..."], "pinned_comment": "...", "cover": {"lines": ["...", "..."], "stamp": "..."}, "trial_hook": "..."}}
After the JSON: the steps as research.md → Steps on screen has them, each with the source it came from (link and date); the screen each line will show and the part it touches; and every number you used with the data id it came from.
```

```text
1 · SEE EACH SCREEN AS IT IS NOW

Describe what they show today: the same names, the same order, the same places. When two sources differ, the newest official one wins. Never draw a screen from memory or from an old video. EPFO's pages often refuse automated reading: open them in a browser.

2 · DESCRIBE EACH SCREEN (reel.json → screens)
{"home": {"device": "laptop", "url": "unifiedportal-mem.epfindia.gov.in/memberinterface", "app": "EPFO Member e-Sewa", "accent": "#1f4e9c",
          "sources": [{"kind": "official", "title": "...", "url": "https://...", "updated": "YYYY-MM-DD", "seen": "YYYY-MM-DD"},

          "parts": [ ...top to bottom... ],
          "overlays": { ... }}}
- "device": "phone" for an app (UMANG) or the portal on a phone, "laptop" for the portal in a browser. "url": the page's address without https://. "app": its name. "accent": the colour of its main buttons.
- "parts", top to bottom, as the screen shows them. Every part a line uses gets an "id": short, lowercase. The kinds the build draws:
  - bar: a phone app's top bar: its title, a back arrow, an action on the right
    {"kind": "bar", "text": "New reel", "action": "Next"}
  - title: the page's name
    {"kind": "title", "text": "My website", "sub": "Data sources · My website"}
  - text: a few lines of the page's own words
    {"kind": "text", "text": "Send events from your server…"}
  - row: a list row: an icon, its words, and a switch ("toggle"), a value ("value": "Off") or an arrow
    {"kind": "row", "id": "schedule", "text": "Schedule", "icon": "clock", "toggle": false}
  - field: a box to type in ("value" when it's filled)
    {"kind": "field", "id": "code", "label": "Test event code", "placeholder": "TEST1234"}
  - button: one button; style primary, secondary, danger, good or link
    {"kind": "button", "id": "save", "text": "Save", "style": "primary"}
  - buttons: buttons side by side
    {"kind": "buttons", "items": [{"id": "partner", "text": "Set up with a partner"}, {"id": "manual", "text": "Set up manually", "style": "link"}]}
  - tabs: tabs under a title
    {"kind": "tabs", "id": "tabs", "items": ["Overview", "Test events", "Settings"], "active": "Overview"}
  - chips: small pills
    {"kind": "chips", "id": "filter", "items": ["All", "Active", "Paused"], "active": "All"}
  - media: a video or photo with its caption box
    {"kind": "media", "text": "Write a caption…"}
  - stat: one status or number, big; tone good, bad or warn
    {"kind": "stat", "id": "server", "label": "Server events", "value": "Not set up", "tone": "bad"}
  - stats: two to four stats side by side
    {"kind": "stats", "items": [{"id": "browser", "label": "Browser events", "value": "Active", "tone": "good"}, {"id": "server", "label": "Server events", "value": "Not set up", "tone": "bad"}]}
  - section: a card on the page with its own parts inside
    {"kind": "section", "id": "capi", "title": "Conversions API", "text": "…", "parts": [...]}
  - table: a table; ✓ and ✗ are drawn as marks
    {"kind": "table", "id": "events", "head": ["Event", "Browser", "Server"], "rows": [["Purchase", "✓", "✓"]]}
  - badge: a small status label
    {"kind": "badge", "id": "dedup", "text": "Deduplicated", "tone": "good"}
  - space: empty room between parts
    {"kind": "space", "h": 24}
  - nav: a laptop page's sidebar
    {"kind": "nav", "id": "nav", "text": "Events Manager", "active": "Data sources", "items": [{"text": "Overview", "icon": "grid"}, {"text": "Data sources", "icon": "server"}]}
  - search: a search box
    {"kind": "search", "id": "find", "placeholder": "Search"}
  - check: a checkbox with its words
    {"kind": "check", "id": "agree", "text": "I agree to the terms", "on": false}
  - steps: a numbered progress list, the first "done" ticked
    {"kind": "steps", "id": "setup", "items": ["Connect", "Verify", "Test"], "done": 1}
- An item of tabs, chips or a sidebar is "<its part's id>/<the item's text>" ("top/Manage"); a table's row is "<the table's id>/<its first cell>".
- "overlays": what opens over the screen, each under its own id:
  - dialog: a box over the dimmed page (on a phone it slides up)
    "partners": {"kind": "dialog", "title": "Choose a partner", "parts": [...]}
  - sheet: a phone's panel from the bottom
    "when": {"kind": "sheet", "title": "Schedule reel", "parts": [...]}
  - menu: a small menu under the part it opens from
    "more": {"kind": "menu", "near": "more_button", "items": [{"id": "edit", "text": "Edit"}, {"id": "delete", "text": "Delete"}]}

    "saved": {"kind": "toast", "text": "Conversions API connected", "tone": "good"}
- Icons for rows and the sidebar: person, pin, clock, gear, search, bell, home, plus, link, chart, check, lock, globe, cart, code, server, browser, eye, calendar, play, share, heart, chat, mail, bolt, doc, shield, user, grid, filter.
- Fill the page as the real one is: every section it shows in that place, in order, with believable example data. NEVER a real person's details: no name but the cast's (Shivam), and every number masked the way the portal masks it, or obviously an example: UAN "XXXX XXXX 1234", mobile "XXXXXX7890", PAN "ABCDE####F", member ID "XX/XXX/0000000/000/0000000". The checks fail any 12-digit or 10-digit number, PAN or member ID in full (E4.28).
- Never draw the EPFO logo, the national emblem or any seal: the build draws only the parts above, so leave logos out of the description (write the portal's name as its title).
- "sources": two at least, one of them "official". "kind": official, video, article, post or forum. "seen": the day you read it, as YYYY-MM-DD. "updated" (a page) or "published" (a video): the date the source shows. At least one source must be dated in the last 60 days, and every one read in the last 30 days.

3 · THE WALK: THE VIEWER SEES EVERY CLICK THAT GETS THEM THERE
The viewer will do this on their own screen, so the reel goes the way they will, click by click. A reel that jumps straight to a button teaches nothing.
- The steps start on the page the viewer sees first when they log in (the member portal's home page; UMANG's EPFO page). Describe that page too, in screens, from its sources.
- From there, every page the reel shows is opened on screen: a tap on the menu item, tab, link or button that opens it, with "go": that page's screen. The member portal's top menu is a tabs part ("top": Home, View, Manage, Account, Online Services) whose items open a menu overlay: {"tap": "top/Manage", "open": "manage", "on": "Manage"}, then {"tap": "markexit", "go": "exit", "on": "Mark"}. A menu that expands first is opened ("open"), then its item is tapped.
- Never start a line on a page nobody opened, never tap a menu item without going to its page, and never tap the page the viewer is already on. The checks fail all three (E4.27). Only the hook and the why before the steps may show any page, and the share line may show the result again.
- A part further down the page: {"scroll": 300} on its word, before the camera goes there.
- On every page that opens, the build shows it whole for a second, then moves in: a line that opens a page gives the new page a moment before its next touch.

4 · WHAT HAPPENS, LINE BY LINE (reel.json → shots)
- A line on a screen: {"type": "screen", "screen": "exit", "focus": "employment", "do": [{"tap": "employment", "open": "jobs", "on": "Employment"}]}
  "focus": the part the line is about: the camera travels there (a lemon ring shows it), then it lifts out big while the rest fades. "do": what happens, each action on its word ("on", copied from the line), in the order the viewer does them.
  - {"tap": id}: tapped. What the tap does goes in the same action: "open": overlay, "close": overlay, "show": a toast, "go": another screen, "toggle": true or false. A row picked in a menu closes it and fills its field at once, so the pick, the close and the field's new value are one action: {"tap": "oldjob", "close": "jobs", "label": "Purani Company", "label_of": "employment", "on": "purani"}.
  - {"write": id, "text": "15/10/2026"}: typed into a field, letter by letter. Never an OTP, a password or a real number: an OTP field is filled with "● ● ● ● ● ●".
  - {"check": id}: a checkbox ticked.
  - {"look": id}: lifted out without a touch, when the line points at it ("Date of Exit khali hai").
  - {"label": "Exit date updated", "label_of": id, "tone": "good"}: a status or value changes, as the portal shows it after the step.
  - {"select": "tabs", "item": "Passbook"}: an item chosen without a tap. {"scroll": 300}: the page scrolls.
  After a "go", the line's next actions happen on the new page: use that page's ids.
- Give every touch its own word; a line with three touches needs words for all three.
- The screen stays from line to line until a card takes its place.
- A line that lands on a result shows it: "label" or "show", on the word that says it.

5 · THE CARDS (the idea behind the screens)
- headline: {"type": "headline", "text": "EXIT DATE KHALI HAI?", "accent": "KHALI HAI?", "at": 0, "in": "none"}
  S01 only, with the screen: the hook's first-frame words, 6 at most. "accent": the end of the headline, on a lemon block.
- route: {"type": "route", "title": "POORA RAASTA", "steps": [{"text": "MANAGE", "sub": "upar ka menu"}, {"text": "MARK EXIT", "sub": "naukri chuno"}], "now": 0}
  The whole path before the first step: 3 to 5 stops of one or two words, each with a short "sub".
- flow: {"type": "flow", "from": [{"title": "Purani company", "sub": "exit date"}], "to": {"title": "EPFO", "sub": "aapka record"},
         "pills": [{"text": "Exit date", "from": 0, "on": "date"}], "result": {"text": "Claim ready", "sub": "transfer bhi", "tone": "good", "on": "ready"}}
  What happens behind the screen: up to 3 senders, one receiver, what travels, and the result: the mistake in red ("tone": "bad"), the fix in green ("good").
- checklist: {"type": "checklist", "title": "MARK EXIT", "sub": "screenshot le lo", "items": [{"text": "Manage, phir Mark Exit"}, {"text": "Sahi naukri chuno"}]}
  The list worth saving: every step in 3 to 5 words, ticked in one after another.
- outro: {"type": "outro", "logo": "PF GURU JI", "tagline": "PF samjho, claim pao.", "web": "@pfguruji"}: the sign-off only. Its words go into card_text.
- The route's chips (reel.json → route): [{"label": "MANAGE", "from": "S03"}, {"label": "OTP", "from": "S07"}]: 5 at most, 12 letters at most each.
A card takes the screen's place for its line (the headline and the screen share S01). Use a card where the line explains, a screen where the line does.

6 · THE SHOTS FOR episode.json
- One shot per script line, with the same ids and chapters.
- The first starts at 0, and each starts where the last one ended. Make each about (words in its line ÷ 2.6) + 0.5 seconds, rounded to 0.1, and the last one 1.5 seconds longer. The build times every shot to the real voice later.
- card_text: every word the shot's cards draw, exactly as drawn. The screens' own words are the portal's: they don't go in card_text. A shot that only shows a screen has an empty card_text. No dash (—) between words on any card.
- uses: the data ids whose numbers the cards show.

CHECK BEFORE YOU ANSWER
- Every screen has two sources or more, one of them official, one dated in the last 60 days, each with its link, "seen" and its date.
- Every menu, tab and button name is written exactly as the newest official page or video shows it.
- Every "focus", "tap", "write", "check" and "look" is an id on its screen (after a "go", on the new one); every "open", "close" and "show" one of its overlays.
- The walk: the steps start on the page the viewer sees first; every later page is opened on screen by the tap that leads there.
- No real person's details anywhere, no logo, no OTP or password on any screen.
- Every "on" word is in that shot's line, and every touch has its own word.
- S01 starts with the headline ("at": 0, "in": "none") and the screen.
- Every string a card draws is in that shot's card_text, character for character.

EPISODE: ep00-focus-sample
```
